scenario_name: Eravikulam National Park approach-road closure (landslide inspection)

trigger.reason: Forest department closes the Eravikulam approach road 09:00-11:30 for a landslide inspection after heavy overnight rain; reopens with restricted single-lane access at 11:30

steps.name: Munnar Town to Eravikulam National Park
Eravikulam National Park (rushed, after 2hr checkpoint wait)

original_plan_for_window.quality_note: Visit cut to 60 of its recommended 120 min after a 2-hour wait at the checkpoint for the landslide inspection to clear — misses much of the Nilgiri Tahr viewing window

recovery_plans.label: Reorder: tea museum and lunch first, full park visit after reopening
recovery_plans.description: Instead of waiting at the checkpoint, spend the closure window at the Tea Museum and over an unhurried lunch in town, then drive up right at the 11:30 reopening for the full recommended visit.

steps.name: Munnar Town to Eravikulam National Park

recovery_plans.tradeoff: Costs 450 more and runs about an hour longer than the original window, but delivers the museum, an unhurried lunch, and the FULL 120-minute park visit instead of a rushed 60-minute one with no wasted wait at the checkpoint.
recovery_plans.best_for: Travelers who prioritize a complete, unrushed Nilgiri Tahr sighting over sticking to a tight schedule

recovery_plans.label: Substitute: skip Eravikulam, do Mattupetty Dam and Echo Point
recovery_plans.description: Drop the park visit for today. Head to Mattupetty Dam and Echo Point instead — a different road, unaffected by the landslide closure.
recovery_plans.tradeoff: Saves 145 rupees and finishes about 95 min earlier; trades the Nilgiri Tahr sanctuary for dam views and a quiet lakeside stop. Eravikulam can be attempted again tomorrow morning.
recovery_plans.best_for: Travelers on a tight schedule or content to skip the Tahr sanctuary

recovery_plans.label: Pivot: full tea-and-spice cultural day with dinner folded in
recovery_plans.description: Since Eravikulam is a morning-only stop, spend the day at the Tea Museum and on a spice-plantation walk, then close with a proper sit-down dinner at Copper Castle instead of a rushed park visit.

baseline_for_comparison.note: Compare against original window (625) plus a separate dinner you'd have paid anyway (~500 at Eastend)

recovery_plans.tradeoff: Costs about 25 more and runs 45 min longer, but replaces a rushed, wait-heavy park visit with a full tea-and-spice cultural day plus a proper sit-down dinner folded in.
recovery_plans.best_for: Travelers who'd rather have a complete cultural day than gamble on a landslide-closure reopening
